name: Austria
keyfacts: Austrian wines are mostly dry whites, with Grüner Veltliner the dominant white grape, and about 30% of wines are red, made from Blaufränkisch, Pinot Noir and Zweigelt.
Districtus Austriae Controllatus (DAC) is the Austrian appellation system, similar to the French AOC, and regional wine committees award it to wines typical of their region.
There are now 18 DACs, starting with Weinviertel DAC from vintage 2002 and including Wachau DAC from vintage 2020.
Zweigelt and Blauburger, both bred at Klosterneuburg in the 1920s, account for nearly half of Austria's red wine.
Mittelburgenland, nicknamed Blaufränkischland, has a red wine DAC for Blaufränkisch, while Weinviertel is the biggest region and holds half the country's Grüner Veltliner.

blurb.text: A above all dry white wine country led by Grüner Veltliner, at 33 percent of vines. About 30 percent of wine is red, from Zweigelt, Blaufränkisch and Pinot Noir. Sweet wines come from around Neusiedler See.
